## Summary
Huizhou Gaoshengda Technology ("GSD", whose site now styles itself Gaoshengda Holdings (Huizhou)) is a wireless-module and IoT-connectivity manufacturer in Huizhou, Guangdong, founded in 1999, whose site names TCL, Lenovo, Midea, Xiaomi, CSOT, Amazon and Roku as customers and claims the largest global share of IoT wireless modules in the TV segment [1]. The IEEE registry holds 54 MA-L blocks (about 906 million addresses) under this name, the first in October 2012 (7C:B2:32) and the newest in August 2025, at No. 75 Zhongkai High-Tech Development District, Huizhou [2][3]. A MAC in one of these blocks is therefore a solder-down or internal-USB module inside somebody else's product, most often a smart TV, and the OUI tells you the module maker, not the brand on the bezel. Documented modules are the WCT6LA2701 (Qualcomm Atheros QCA9378, 2x2 802.11ac plus Bluetooth 4.1, FCC ID 2AC23-WCT6LA2701) [4] and the WF7ERL1500 (MediaTek MT7601U, 1x1 802.11bgn, FCC ID 2AC23WF7E) which DeviWiki records inside VIZIO hardware [5]; DeviWiki also notes that "Hui Zhou Gaoshengda Technology is apparently GSD" [5][6]. Expect 2.4 GHz-only Wi-Fi 4 from older TVs and dual-band Wi-Fi 5 with BLE from newer ones. The company's product pages were not reachable, so the current chipset line-up and any Wi-Fi 6 parts are not documented here, and no MAC-randomization behaviour or security advisories were found for the modules.
